description: Use of the Purdue AF agentic interface (MCP server): who is using it, what they use it for, and whether it works. Private instance — panels name individual users.

panels.description: Distinct users who called a tool in the selected range.
panels.title: Active users

panels.description: All tool invocations in the range.
panels.title: Tool calls

panels.description: Calls that started, stopped or resized something: create dask cluster, scale dask cluster, stop dask cluster, start af session, stop af session, restart af session.
panels.title: Facility changes

panels.description: Share of tool calls that returned a result. needs_input counts as success — the agent was told what to ask for.
panels.title: Success rate

panels.description: Tool calls that failed because a backend did — the facility's fault, not the caller's.
panels.title: Upstream errors

panels.description: 95th percentile across all tools.
panels.title: p95 latency

panels.description: Tool calls grouped by what they act on, so a session spent managing Dask reads as one band instead of eight overlapping tool names. Ungrouped means a tool exists that this dashboard does not know about.
panels.title: Activity by area

panels.description: One row per user over the selected range. Bars compare users within a column, so the longest bar under Dask clusters is the heaviest Dask user.
panels.title: Who works on what

panels.description: Individual tools, for when the area breakdown is not specific enough.
panels.title: Busiest tools

panels.description: Only the calls that mutate state. A flat line here with activity above means agents were reading, not changing.
panels.title: Facility changes over time

panels.description: Top 10 users in the range.
panels.title: Tool calls by user

panels.description: Calls that returned an error, by user. user_error is usually a malformed request from the agent; upstream_error is ours.
panels.title: Failed calls by user

panels.description: success and needs_input are healthy; user_error is a bad request; upstream_error and exception are the facility's.
panels.title: Outcomes

panels.description: Which tool is failing, and how.
panels.title: Failures by tool

panels.description: Slow tools are usually waiting on a backend — compare with upstream latency.
panels.title: Tool latency p95

panels.description: Per backend.
